rationales.A: Taney never resigned; the split was in the Democratic Party, not the Court.
rationales.B: Lincoln led the Republicans, who already opposed Lecompton; the split was among Democrats.
rationales.C: Background from the books: Douglas said the Lecompton vote was unfair, broke with Buchanan, and joined Republicans to block admission.
rationales.D: Background from the books: the Southerners stayed; it was Douglas and the Northern Democrats who broke with Buchanan.
rationales.general:
1. See Buchanan’s stand: he staked his presidency on admitting Kansas under Lecompton.
2. See Douglas’s break: the vote gave Kansans no fair choice, so he opposed his own president.
3. See the split: Northern Democrats joined Republicans, and the party cracked before 1860.
Remember: when a president demands loyalty to an unfair vote, he can split his own party.
